hindi: अब इसके बाद हम दिनचर्या-अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the daily routine (dinacaryā).

words.gram: n. acc. sg. used as ind.

hindi: स्वस्थ व्यक्ति आयु की रक्षा के लिए ब्राह्म मुहूर्त में उठे, पाचन और अपाचन का विचार करता हुआ, और वेग उत्पन्न होने पर त्याग करे।
english: A healthy person should rise at the Brāhma muhūrta (the pre-dawn period), examining digestion and non-digestion, and, for the protection of life, should void when the urge has arisen.
notes: The object of samutsṛjet (urine and stool) is given in the next unit. "Brāhma muhūrta" is taken as the pre-dawn period; the text itself does not define it. "jīrṇājīrṇe" is read as an accusative dual dvandva, object of nirūpayan; the text does not say "food" (it is understood).

hindi: उत्तर की ओर मुख करके, और रात में दक्षिण की ओर मुख करके, वाणी को रोके हुए, झुका हुआ, अंगों को ढके हुए और आवृत किए हुए व्यक्ति मूत्र और मल का त्याग करे।
english: Facing north, and at night facing south, restraining speech, bowed, with the limbs covered and veiled over, one should void urine and stool.
notes: The verb samutsṛjet is in the previous unit. The text says only "facing north" and, for the night, "facing south"; the contrast with daytime is implied by the sentence, not stated. "avaguṇṭhita" (veiled) is not said to mean the head; the head is a common understanding but not in the Sanskrit.

words.gloss: on impure ground, road, earth, ash, cow-stall, ground strewn with cow-dung

hindi: जो वेग स्वयं चल पड़ा हो, उसे निकलने दे, परन्तु प्रयत्न करके उसे बाहर न निकाले। और अपवित्र स्थान, मार्ग, मिट्टी, राख, गोशाला तथा गोबर बिखरे हुए स्थान पर मल-मूत्र त्याग न करे।
english: One should let out what has begun to move, but should not force it out with effort. And [one should] not [void] on impure ground, a road, earth, ash, a cow-stall, or ground strewn with cow-dung,
notes: The verb of the second line is understood from the previous units (samutsṛjet). The long locative compound is read as a list: amedhya, mārga, mṛd, bhasma, go-sthāna, ākīrṇa-gomaya. It could also be read with "ākīrṇa" (strewn) governing the whole list, or with "mṛd" in another sense; the book's own split was followed. The sentence continues in the next unit.

hindi: भय या असमर्थता की स्थिति को छोड़कर, इच्छा से भूमि को ढके बिना (पाठ अनिश्चित) मल-मूत्र त्याग न करे। वेग होने पर दूसरे कार्य में न लगा रहे, और साध्य रोग को जीते बिना भी न रहे।
english: Nor [should one void] willingly without having covered the ground (conjectural reading), except in fear or incapacity. One with an urge should not be occupied with other work, nor [be so] without having overcome a curable disease.

Alternative: "tiraskṛtya" could mean "disregarding/slighting" the ground, giving a different sense. The second line is elliptical: the second "na ... ajitvā" clause is read as "nor [be occupied with other things] without having overcome a curable disease"; the book commentary is not followed. hindi: मल के मार्ग को शल्य (काँटे या बाहरी कण) से रहित और दोषरहित मिट्टी के ढेलों से पोंछकर, निकाले हुए स्वच्छ जलों और मिट्टियों से उसका उपचार करे।
english: With the excretory passage wiped by lumps of earth free of śalya (splinters or foreign bodies) and unspoiled, one should treat it with clean waters that have been drawn up, and with earths,
notes: "mala-ayana" (path of the excreta) is taken as the anal/urinary passage; the text does not say which. "abhyuddhṛta" is read as "drawn up/taken up" (e.g. from a source); "yojayet" is rendered "treat/apply" and its object is understood. The sentence continues into the next unit (śaucam).

words.gram: karmadhāraya (neg. an-upatita + bindu), m. inst. pl.

hindi: ऐसी शुद्धि करे जो लेप और दुर्गन्ध को दूर करे, जिसमें जल की बूँदें न गिरें। और धातुओं, मलों, आँसू, नेत्र तथा गिरे हुए केश और नखों का स्पर्श करके,
english: a cleansing that removes smear and odour, with drops not falling; and having touched the dhātus, impurities (malas), tears, the eye, and fallen hair and nails,
notes: "anupatita-bindubhiḥ" is read as an-upatita ("with drops not falling", i.e. not dripping/splashing); if anupatita is read as "following/falling in succession" the sense would be the opposite. The verb for the second line is in the next unit (ācāmet, "should sip water"). "dhātūn" is left as dhātu: the text does not say whether bodily constituents or minerals are meant. "dṛśam" is a singular accusative "eye".

hindi: स्नान करके, भोजन की इच्छा होने पर, भोजन करके, सोकर, छींककर, देवताओं की पूजा में, अथवा मार्ग को पार करके, उत्तर की ओर मुख करके बैठा हुआ व्यक्ति आचमन करे।
english: After bathing, when wishing to eat, after eating, after sleeping, after sneezing, in the worship of the gods, or after passing over a road, one should sip water (ācamana), seated facing north.

words.gloss: reaching the base of the thumb

hindi: अथवा पूर्व की ओर मुख करके, एकान्त स्थान में बैठा हुआ, (हाथ) घुटनों के बाहर न रखे हुए, दूसरी ओर न देखता हुआ, बिना बोले, उत्तरीय वस्त्र धारण किए हुए, स्वच्छ और अँगूठे की जड़ तक पहुँचने वाले जलों से आचमन करे।
english: Or facing east, staying in a secluded place, [with the hands] not outside the knees, not looking elsewhere, not talking, wearing an upper garment, [one should sip] with clean [waters] reaching the base of the thumb.
notes: "hands" in "not outside the knees" is supplied from the usual understanding; the Sanskrit has only "bahirjānu". The nouns "waters" and "should sip" are understood (jalaiḥ comes in the next unit; ācāmet in the previous). "svacchaiḥ ... gaiḥ" is an instrumental plural qualifying those waters.
lines_deva: प्राङ्मुखो वा विविक्तस्थो न बहिर्जानु नान्यदृक् ॥

hindi: न उठाए हुए जलों से, न झुककर, न ऊपर की ओर; न आग पर पके हुए और न दुर्गन्धयुक्त जलों से; न झाग, बुलबुलों या क्षार वाले जलों से, और न एक हाथ से दिए हुए जलों से आचमन करे।
english: Not with waters lifted up, not bent over, not upward; not with waters heated by fire, nor foul-smelling; not with waters having foam, bubbles or alkaline quality, nor with waters offered with one hand.
notes: Unclear points (editors flagged "uddhṛta"): uddhṛta may mean water lifted/scooped up, or taken out; "nānato" is read as na + ānataḥ ("not bent"); the book's na + anataḥ ("not unbent") would reverse the sense. "nordhvam" (not upward) is rendered literally: it may refer to the posture or to the water. "ācāmet" and "jalaiḥ" are understood from the neighbouring units.

hindi: एक हाथ गीला रखकर न करे, अपवित्र हाथ-पैरों से न करे, और शब्द करता हुआ न करे। वट, असन, अर्क, खदिर, करंज और कवीर से उत्पन्न
english: Not with one hand wet, not with impure hands and feet, and not making sound; [a tooth-cleaning stick] born of vaṭa, asana, arka, khadira, karañja and kavīra,
notes: The second line begins the list of trees for the tooth-cleaning stick (dantadhāvana is the object, in unit 15). The tree names are kept as names; no identification is made. "kavīra" may be a variant for another name; kept as printed.

words.gloss: born of sarja, arimeda, apāmārga, mārutī, kakubha (plant names)

hindi: सर्ज, अरिमेद, अपामार्ग, मारुती और ककुभ से उत्पन्न; कषाय, तिक्त या कटु; अथवा ऐसी ही कोई अन्य मूल भी।
english: Born of sarja, arimeda, apāmārga, mārutī and kakubha; astringent, bitter or pungent; or any other root of this kind as well.
notes: Names kept as names. "mūla" (root) is rendered literally; whether it means the root of the plant or the source is not stated. The split arimeda (sarja-arimeda) follows the book; "sarjāri-meda" is also possible.

words.gloss: of thickness equal to the tip of the little finger

hindi: जिसका रस ज्ञात हो, जिसका अग्रभाग कुचला हुआ हो, जो सीधा और गाँठ रहित हो, अच्छी भूमि में उत्पन्न हो; जिसकी मोटाई कनिष्ठा अँगुली के अग्रभाग के समान हो, जो भली-भाँति बनाया गया हो और बारह अँगुल का हो।
english: Of known taste, with the tip crushed, straight, without knots, grown in good soil; of a thickness equal to the tip of the little finger, well made, twelve fingers [long].
notes: The noun they qualify (dantadhāvana) is given in the next unit. "kṣuṇṇāgra" (tip crushed) is read as the tip chewed/crushed into a brush; the Sanskrit only says crushed. "dvādaśāṅgula" is taken as length.

hindi: तब उसी से धीरे-धीरे दाँतों और मसूड़ों को कष्ट न पहुँचाते हुए घिसे, और जीभ को जीभ खुरचने के साधन से सुखपूर्वक खुरचे।

hindi: अपच, वमन, श्वास, खाँसी, ज्वर और अर्दित से पीड़ित, तथा प्यास, मुख के पाक और हृदय, नेत्र, सिर और कान के रोगों वाला व्यक्ति उसे न चबाए।
english: One suffering from indigestion, vomiting, śvāsa, cough, fever or ardita, and one with thirst, mouth-pāka, or ailments of the heart, eye, head or ear, should not eat (chew) that.
notes: "tat" is read as the tooth-cleaning stick. "adyāt" literally "should eat"; "chew" is the sense here. hindi: मीठा, खट्टा, नमकीन, सूखा, खोखला, दुर्गन्धयुक्त और चिपचिपा भी नहीं; पालाश, आसन — आसन-वृक्ष की लकड़ी का, अथवा बैठने का आसन — दन्तधावन और पादुकाएँ छोड़ दे।
english: Nor one that is sweet, sour or salty, dry, hollow, foul-smelling or slimy; one should avoid what is of palāśa, (āsana: of asana wood, or: a seat), the tooth-cleaning stick and a pair of sandals.
notes: "pālāśam āsanaṃ" can be read as two parallel adjectives (of palāśa, of asana) qualifying dantadhāvanam, or as 'palāśa' governing all three nouns with āsana 'a seat'; the singular adjective with a dual noun (pāduke) is loose. "tyajet" probably also governs the earlier accusatives. Sweet-sour-salty qualities are the opposite of those recommended in unit 13.

words.gloss: with the mouth full of water

hindi: पहले नीचे के दाँतों को घिसे; प्रातःकाल मुँह में जल भरकर दोनों आँखों को सींचे, ग्रीष्म और शरद ऋतु में ठंडे जल से।
english: One should first rub the lower teeth; in the morning, with the mouth filled with water, one should sprinkle the two eyes, in summer and autumn with cold water.
notes: "pūrvam adhaḥ" is read as "first the lower [teeth]"; it could also mean "first downward". "grīṣma-śaradoḥ" (summer and autumn) is read with "śītavāriṇā", the cold water; it may govern the whole sprinkling.

hindi: देवताओं और वृद्धजनों को प्रणाम करके, शुभ मंगल-अष्टशत (एक सौ आठ माना गया; संख्या अनिश्चित) सुनते हुए, उसके तुरंत बाद घी को देखे, जो (पाठ खंडित होने से अनिश्चित, संभवतः सोने के पात्र में) रखा हो।
english: Having bowed to the gods and the elders, listening to the auspicious maṅgala-aṣṭa-śata (taken as 108 auspicious things; the count is uncertain), one should immediately afterwards look at ghee placed in [gold? the text is damaged here].

text_flags.why: possible: "kāṃ ghanā-" is not a word; the editors suggest kāñcana-vinyastaṃ ("placed in gold"). The syllable count is the same (16) either way, which fits the suggestion; the reading remains conjectural

notes: Second line is damaged (editors flagged it): the reading "placed in gold [vessel]" is conjectural, hence the Hindi and English wording "golden vessel" is not firm. "maṅgalāṣṭaśata" is read as "the 108 auspicious (things)" (aṣṭa-śata = 108); the text does not say whether names, verses or objects. The book English "hundreds of auspicious words" is not supported.

hindi: फिर प्रतिदिन नेत्रों के लिए हितकारी सौवीर अंजन का प्रयोग करे। उससे दोनों नेत्र मनोहर और सूक्ष्म दृष्टि वाले हो जाते हैं।
english: Then one should use daily sauvīra collyrium, beneficial for the eyes. By it the two eyes become pleasing and of fine sight.
notes: "sauvīra" is kept as a substance name and not identified.

hindi: वे स्पष्ट तीन रंगों वाले, निर्मल, और अत्यन्त चिकनी तथा घनी पलकों के बालों वाले हो जाते हैं। नेत्र तेज से युक्त है; उसे विशेष रूप से कफ से भय है।
english: They become of three distinct colours, clear, and with very smooth and dense lashes. The eye consists of tejas (fire, radiance); for it the danger is especially from Kapha.
notes: The first line continues the dual subject of the previous unit (the two eyes become ...). "tejomaya" is rendered "consisting of tejas"; "śleṣmataḥ" is Kapha (śleṣman). The three colours are not specified in the text.

words.gloss: in seven nights, at seven-night intervals
on this account, from this (or: after this)

words.gram: n. acc. sg. used as ind.

hindi: इस कारण (अथवा इसके बाद) सात रातों के अन्तर से स्रावण के लिए रसांजन का प्रयोग करे। फिर अणु तैल का नस्य, फिर गण्डूष धारण करे।
english: On this account (asmāt; or: after this), at seven-night intervals one should apply rasāñjana for the purpose of causing discharge; then aṇu oil as nasya (nasal administration), then holding a gaṇḍūṣa (mouthful of liquid).
notes: "saptarātre" is read as "in seven nights, i.e. once in seven nights", and "asmāt" as "on this account" or "after this" (the Hindi and English now give both); neither is certain. "srāvaṇa" is rendered literally as "causing discharge"; the text does not say of what. Substance and preparation names are kept as names. The verb for the second line is understood (yojayet/kuryāt).

words.gloss: (those whose) skin, shoulders, neck, face, chest are firm, raised, clear

hindi: उनकी त्वचा, कंधे, गर्दन, मुख और छाती सुदृढ़, उठे हुए और प्रसन्न होते हैं; उनके मुख सुगंधित, स्वर स्निग्ध और इंद्रियाँ निर्मल होती हैं।
english: Their skin, shoulders, neck, face and chest are firm, raised and clear; their mouths are fragrant, their voices smooth, and their sense organs clear.
notes: The subject (the people described) is not named in this unit; the following unit names the nasya-habituated (nasya-śīlinaḥ), so the description belongs to them. snigdha 'smooth/unctuous' is rendered 'smooth' for the voice; prasanna 'clear/bright' for the skin etc.

words.gloss: free of wrinkles, grey hair, blemishes
lip-cracking, roughness, dry mouth, tooth diseases

hindi: नस्य का सेवन करने के अभ्यस्त लोग झुर्रियों, पके बालों और धब्बों से रहित हो जाते हैं; और होंठों का फटना, रूखापन, मुख का सूखना तथा दाँतों के रोग उन्हें नहीं होते।
english: Those who are habituated to nasya become free of wrinkles, grey hair and blemishes; and cracking of the lips, roughness, dryness of the mouth and diseases of the teeth do not occur.
notes: The verb 'na syuḥ' of the second line is in the next unit (29, first line) and is supplied in the translation. vyaṅga = a (facial) blemish or discolouration; dvija ('twice-born') = tooth; āmaya = disease. The unit's two lines together with 29.1 form one sentence.

words.gloss: holding a mouthful of water of khadira, milky trees, arimeda

hindi: स्नेह का गंडूष मुख में धारण करने से स्वर की क्षतियाँ नहीं होतीं। खदिर, क्षीरिवृक्षों और अरिमेद के जल के कवल को मुख में धारण करना—
english: And injuries of the voice would not occur from holding an oily mouthful (sneha-gaṇḍūṣa) in the mouth. The holding of a mouthful (kavala) of the water of khadira, the kṣīrivṛkṣa (milky trees) and arimeda—
notes: Sentence continues in unit 30: kavala-grahaḥ is the subject of the participle prasekajit there. khadira and arimeda are drug names, kṣīrivṛkṣa 'milky (latex) trees': names kept, no identification. I take arimeda as one drug name (the book splits ari-meda). 'ambu' (water) is read with the compound 'water of khadira, ...'; whether this means a decoction is not stated.

words.gloss: overcoming loss of appetite, distaste of mouth, foulness of impurity, excess salivation
with mouthfuls of pleasantly warm water

hindi: वह अरुचि, मुख की विरसता, मल की दुर्गंध और लार के अधिक स्राव को जीतने वाला है; और सुखद रूप से गुनगुने जल के गंडूषों से मुख में हल्कापन उत्पन्न होता है।
english: It (the holding of the mouthful) overcomes loss of appetite, distaste in the mouth, foulness from impurity and excessive flow of saliva; and from mouthfuls of pleasantly warm water, lightness of the mouth arises.
notes: prasekajit is a nominative adjective agreeing with kavala-grahaḥ of unit 29. mala-pūti: 'foulness of impurity' (alternatively 'foul impurities'); praseka = flow, here salivation. 'Lightness' of the mouth (vaktra-lāghava) is kept literal.

hindi: इसके बाद प्रयोग के योग्य धूम तथा गंध, माला आदि का आचरण करे। धूम से इसके जत्रु के ऊपर उत्पन्न होने वाले वात और कफ के रोग नहीं होते।
english: Then one should practise the smoke suited to regular use, and perfumes, garlands and the like. By the smoke, for him, diseases of vāta and kapha arising above the collar-bone (jatru) do not occur.
notes: prāyogika is rendered 'suited to regular use' (literally 'of application'); the text itself does not say more here. jatru = the collar-bone region.

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, pp. n. acc. sg. ut-√kliś (caus.)

words.gloss: set in motion by nasal administration

hindi: अंजन से उभारे हुए को नस्यों से, और नावन से प्रेरित को कवलों से—
english: What has been stirred up by collyrium, by nasyas; what has been set in motion by nasal administration, by mouthfuls (kavala)—
notes: Elliptical: the verb and object (jayet, vāta-kapham) come in unit 33. Reading: each condition is dealt with by the next measure in order. Alternative: the instrumentals could name what stirs up, not what overcomes; the sequence in 33 (kramāt, 'in order') favours the reading given. The unit is one printed half-verse of 16 syllables; the other half of this verse is the first half-line of unit 33. See GROUPING in 33.

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, pp. n. acc. sg. ut-√kliś

hindi: कवल से उभारे हुए को धूम से, क्रम से वात और कफ को जीते। गंध, माला आदि पौरुषवर्धक हैं, अलक्ष्मी का नाश करने वाले हैं और शृंगार हैं।
english: What has been stirred up by mouthfuls, by smoke: in order one should overcome vāta and kapha. Perfumes, garlands and the like promote virility, destroy misfortune, and are an adornment.
notes: GROUPING: this unit (typed 'prose') is really two half-verse lines printed as one. (a) 'dhūmena ... jayet' (16 syllables) is the second half of the verse begun in unit 32 (32 + first half of 33). (b) 'gandhamālyādikaṃ vṛṣyam alakṣmīghnaṃ prasādhanam' (16 syllables) is a separate half-verse, a statement about perfumes and garlands; it is not completed by what follows (unit 34 begins a new topic, clothing). Elided object in (a): the doṣa stirred up by kavala is dealt with by smoke.
lines_deva: धूमेन कवलोत्क्लिष्टं क्रमाद्वातकफंजयेत् गंधमाल्यादिकं वृष्यमलक्ष्मीघ्नं प्रसाधनं ॥
lines_iast: dhūmena kavalotkliṣṭaṃ kramādvātakaphaṃjayet gaṃdhamālyādikaṃ vṛṣyamalakṣmīghnaṃ prasādhanaṃ ||

hindi: जीर्ण, मैला, लाल या भड़कीला वस्त्र धारण न करे; माला न लटकती हुई हो, न बाहर की ओर हो, न लाल हो, केवल जल में उत्पन्न होने वाले पुष्पों को छोड़कर।
english: One should not wear a garment that is worn out, dirty, red or showy; nor a garland that hangs low, nor outside, nor red, except water-born (flowers).
notes: 'na bahiḥ' is ambiguous ('not outside', e.g. not worn outwardly on the garment); kept literal. 'jalajāt ṛte' read as 'except water-born (flowers)' (jalaja = water-born, such as lotus). ulbaṇa = excessive/conspicuous. The verb dhārayet of the first line governs mālyam too. The sentence continues into unit 35, line 1.
lines_deva: माल्यं न लंबं न बहिर्न रक्तं जलजादृते ॥
lines_iast: mālyaṃ na laṃbaṃ na bahirna raktaṃ jalajādṛte ||

hindi: और दूसरे के द्वारा पहना हुआ वस्त्र, फूल या जूते भी धारण न करे। रुचि, निर्मलता और सुगंध की इच्छा करने वाला मुख में धारण करे—
english: Nor should one wear cloth, a flower or a pair of sandals already worn by another. One who desires relish, clarity and fragrance should hold in the mouth—
notes: GROUPING: line 1 ('naiva ... upānahau') completes the prohibition begun in unit 34 (dhārayet governs it; the three half-lines 34.1, 34.2, 35.1 make one sentence). Line 2 starts a new sentence whose object is in unit 36 (the tāmbūlī leaf with pūga-fruit etc.), so 35.2 + 36 belong together. The object of 'dhārayet' in line 2 is not in this unit.

words.gloss: drug names: jātī, lavaṅga, karpūra, kaṅkola, kaṭuka

hindi: जाती, लवंग, कर्पूर, कंकोल और कटुक के साथ, ताम्बूली की कोमल पत्ती, मनोहर, पूग के फल सहित।
english: Together with jātī, lavaṅga, karpūra, kaṅkola and kaṭuka: the tender leaf of the tāmbūlī, pleasing, accompanied by pūga-fruit.
notes: Continues from unit 35.2 ('one should hold in the mouth ...'). All names are kept as drug names, none identified. 'kaṭuka' may be a drug name or the adjective 'pungent' (the editors' note says the book's Hindi/English glosses of this item conflict); I treat it as a drug name, doubtful. tāmbūlī is a plant name, kept. This unit has no verb of its own; 'hold in the mouth' (dhārayet) is carried from 35.2.

words.gloss: of those with raktapitta, wounded, wasted, dry, or irritated-eyed
of those afflicted by poison, fainting, intoxication

hindi: वह रक्तपित्त के रोगियों, क्षत से ग्रस्त, क्षीण, रूखे तथा कुपित नेत्रों वाले लोगों के लिए, और विष, मूर्च्छा तथा मद से पीड़ित लोगों के लिए और शोष के रोगियों के लिए अपथ्य है।
english: That is unsuitable for those with raktapitta, the wounded, the wasted, the dry, and those with irritated eyes; and for those afflicted by poison, fainting or intoxication, and for those with śoṣa (wasting).
notes: 'tat' presumably refers to the preparation described in units 35-36 (not named in this unit). raktapitta = the named disorder ('blood-pitta'); śoṣa = drying up/wasting; kept literal. 'kṣata-kṣīṇa' may instead be one pair ('wasted by injury'); I split them as separate items. Printed 'rukṣa' is read as rūkṣa (dry).

hindi: सोकर उठे हुए, भोजन किए हुए, स्नान किए हुए और वमन किए हुए मनुष्य के लिए वह हितकर है— दो पत्ते, एक पूग, और चूर्ण तथा खदिर सहित।
english: That is suitable for a person who has risen from sleep, eaten, bathed or vomited: a pair of leaves, one pūga, and with powder and khadira.
notes: 'tat' (that) is presumably the tāmbūlī preparation of the preceding units. pūga and khadira are plant names, kept. cūrṇa is rendered 'powder' (not specified further).
lines_deva: पथ्यं सुप्तोत्थिते भुक्ते स्नाते वांते च मानवे ॥
द्विपत्रमेकं पूगं च सचूर्णखदिरं च तत् ॥

dvipatramekaṃ pūgaṃ ca sacūrṇakhadiraṃ ca tat ||

words.gloss: one should rise up, set to work
for the sake of wealth (conjectural; printed 'syarthaṃ')

hindi: इसके बाद— पाठ क्षतिग्रस्त है; अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार— धन के लिए, धन से जुड़े कार्यों में उद्यत हो। जिसके साधन पास न हों, ऐसी दीर्घ आयु भी निंदित है।
english: Then [conjectural reading; the printed text is damaged] one should set to work for the sake of wealth, in pursuits connected with wealth. Even a long life is censured when the means (of living) are not at hand.

text_flags.why: possible: printed 'tato'syarthaṃ' is not construable; 'tato'rthārtham' (then, for wealth) fits the sense (artha-theme of the next half-verse) and the 16-syllable count.
possible: the initial 'm' belongs to the preceding word (arthārtham + artheṣu); 'artheṣv arthānubandhiṣu' = in pursuits connected with wealth.

The reading 'uttiṣṭheta tato 'rthārtham artheṣv arthānubandhiṣu' is a conjecture that restores sense and metre (16 syllables) and matches the book's own suggestion. Line 2 is clear. hindi: धन की इच्छा करने वाला उपायों से कृषि, वाणिज्य, गोरक्षा और गुणवान् राजा का आश्रय ले, और ऐसे कर्म का भी जो दोनों लोकों के विरुद्ध न हो।
english: One who desires wealth should resort, by means, to agriculture, trade, cattle-keeping and a virtuous king, and to an occupation not opposed to both worlds.

text_flags.why: possible: aviruddham is neuter/masculine but kriyām is feminine; either read adverbially (as I did) or emend to feminine -āṃ.

english: Having released the urges (vega), and [text unclear: 'gamanakhamāhārasamāstriyaḥ'], one should go out, having taken hold of, with the hand, the gods, the revered, ghee and auspicious things.

words.gloss: looking only a yoke's length ahead

hindi: छाता और पादत्राण सहित, जुए भर की दूरी तक दृष्टि रखते हुए चले; और रात में, अत्यधिक आवश्यक कार्य होने पर, दंड, शिरोभूषण और साथी सहित चले।
english: With umbrella and footwear, looking a yoke's length ahead, one should walk about; and at night, when the business is exceedingly pressing, with a staff, a head-dress and a companion.
notes: yuga-mātra = the measure of a yoke (its length is not given here). maulin (from mauli) = having a crown/topknot/head-dress; rendered 'head-dress', ambiguous. 'ca' links the night rule to the day rule; 'vicaret' is understood in the second line.

words.gloss: shadows of caityas, revered ones, banners, ill-regarded things; ashes, husks, impure things

hindi: रात में ढककर घूमे, दिन में सिर ढककर नहीं। चैत्य, पूज्यजन, ध्वजा और निंदित वस्तुओं की छायाएँ, तथा भस्म, भूसी और अशुद्ध वस्तुएँ—
english: At night one should go about covered; by day, not with the head covered. The shadows of caityas (sacred shrines or trees), revered ones, banners and ill-regarded things, and ashes, husks and impure things—
notes: 'śiraḥ' may be shared by both prāvṛtya (head covered at night, not by day), or the first prāvṛtya may have no stated object; the English 'covered' keeps both open. In the compound, chāyā may govern only the preceding members or the whole group; I read 'shadows of caitya, pūjya, dhvaja, aśasta' and then ashes, husks, impure things. The governing verb (ākramet) is in unit 44. aśasta = condemned/ill-regarded (persons or things).
lines_deva: प्रावृत्य पर्यटेद्रात्रौ न प्रावृत्य शिरो ऽहनि ॥

words.gloss: ground of gravel, clods, offerings, bathing

english: One should not step upon these, nor on ground of gravel, clods, bali-offerings or bathing. At midday, at the two twilights, at night, at midnight—a crossroads—

hindi: शिव, पूज्य, प्रशस्तों और मंगल वस्तुओं पर हुंकार न करे। उनकी अपसव्य रूप से परिक्रमा न करे, और दूसरी वस्तुओं की दक्षिण का अनुसरण करते हुए परिक्रमा न करे।
english: One should not utter 'huṃ' at Śiva, at the venerable, at the praised ones, or at auspicious things. One should not go around (them) left-wise (apasavya), nor the others following the right (anudakṣiṇa).

words.gloss: restlessness of hands, speech, feet, stick, eyes, belly

english: Because abhyaṅga is supremely good for the skin, therefore one should practise it. One should practise it especially on the head, ears and feet.

destroying pain of jaw, nape, head and ear

dispelling numbness of the feet, fatigue, stiffness, contraction, cracking

The translation of line 1 is tentative (mānitā read as pride; unresolved, the verse has no verb). 'jīviteśvaryya' is read jīvita + īśvarya (īśvarya as printed; the book reads aiśvarya). 'yānaṃ dhūmaṃ' could be 'going through smoke'; I keep the two words separate. 'śavāśraya' = taking recourse to / staying by a corpse. śavāśrayaṃ agrees in case, number and gender with dhūmaṃ, so it may qualify it ('smoke connected with a corpse'); the translation keeps two items, unsettled.

uncertain.note: [src/hindi] Hindi says "नाश करने वाले कार्य छोड़ें", English says "avoid boasting"; verse has no verb — suggested: `मानिता` = pride; unresolved

hindi: मद्य में अत्यधिक आसक्ति तथा स्त्रियों के विषय में विश्वास और स्वतंत्रता को छोड़ दे। जिस वास्तु की उसके शास्त्र ने निंदा की हो, उसमें एक दिन भी न रहे।
english: One should avoid excessive attachment to liquor, and trust and independence towards women. One should not live even for a single day in a building site (vāstu) condemned by its treatise.
notes: 'tyajet' here probably governs the open lists of units 108-111 as well. 'strīṣu' with visrambha-svātantrye: trust and independence (given) to/among women. 'tat-śāstra' = the treatise of that subject (on vāstu); 'tat' refers back to vāstu. 'ekāham' = for one day. Line 2 is a separate sentence; the verse mixes two topics.

hindi: न रोगों की बहुलता वाले देश में, न वैद्यरहित और न नायकरहित देश में; न उस स्थान में जहाँ अधर्मी लोग अधिक हों, न उपद्रव से ग्रस्त स्थान में और न पर्वतीय स्थान में रहे।
english: Nor in a region abounding in disease, nor in one without a physician, nor in one without a leader; nor in one that is mostly full of unrighteous people, nor in one beset by affliction, nor in a mountain region.
notes: The verb 'adhivaset' (live in) is carried over from unit 112 line 2. 'nādharmi janabhūyiṣṭhaṃ' is one compound split by a space in the print: adharmi-jana-bhūyiṣṭha 'mostly (made up of) unrighteous people'. 'upasṛṣṭa' = afflicted (by calamity, disturbance); the text does not say what kind. 'avaidya' read as 'lacking a physician'.

words.gloss: where water, remedies, kindling, flowers, grass, fuel are abundant
words.gram: bahuvrīhi (prājya- qualifying a dvandva), n. loc. sg., qualifying pure

words.gloss: with outskirts rich in food, secure, delightful

hindi: जहाँ जल, औषध, समिधा, फूल, घास और ईंधन प्रचुर हों, वहाँ रहे; ऐसे नगर में जिसके आसपास का क्षेत्र अन्न से समृद्ध, सुरक्षित और रमणीय हो तथा जो पंडितों से सुशोभित हो।
english: One should dwell where water, remedies, kindling sticks, flowers, grass and fuel are abundant, in a city whose outskirts are rich in food, secure and delightful, and which is adorned by scholars.
notes: 'prājya' (abundant) is taken to qualify the whole locative dvandva. 'samit' = kindling stick (sacrificial fuel). 'subhikṣa-kṣema-ramyānte' is read as a bahuvrīhi 'whose anta (edge, surroundings) is rich in food, safe and pleasant'; it could also be read 'at the delightful end/border'. The words qualify 'pure'.

words.gloss: of men and gods (emended; the printed narāmasrāṇāṃ is not a word)

hindi: मनुष्यों और देवताओं की, सिद्धों की और शास्त्रों की निंदा न करने वाला, त्रिवर्ग का तथा यथोचित रूप से लोगों का आराधक बने।
english: Not scornful of men and gods, of the siddhas and of the treatises, one should be a cultivator of the trivarga (the triad of aims) and, as is fitting, of people.

text_flags.why: 'narāmasrāṇām' is not a word (and the book's split 'nara-amastra' is also unnatural); nara-amarāṇām 'of men and gods' fits the series 'siddhānām śāstrāṇām' and keeps the same syllable count; the s is probably a stray letter (possible)

notes: Emended reading nara-amarāṇām (men and gods) used for the translation. The book's 'human laws'/'astras' do not fit. 'trivarga' is conventionally dharma, artha, kāma, but the verse does not name them. 'ārādhaka' = one who serves/pleases/pursues.

uncertain.note: [src/split] `नरामस्राणां` / split `नर-अमस्त्राणां` non-word; Hindi "अस्त्रों", English "human laws" both off — suggested: `नरामराणां` (men and gods)

hindi: दस धर्ममार्गों की रक्षा करता हुआ भीतरी शत्रुओं को जीते। हिंसा, चोरी, अनुचित कामना, चुगली, कठोर वाणी और असत्य —
english: Guarding the ten paths of dharma, one should conquer the inner enemies. Violence, theft, wrong desire, slander, harsh speech and falsehood --

text_flags.why: possible: read as jayet + nābhyantarān the sense would be 'should not conquer inner enemies', contradicting the context; jayet + ābhyantarān gives jayed ābhyantarān, so the n is probably stray (the syllable count is the same either way)

notes: The second line begins the list of the ten sinful actions, which continues in unit 117 (the usual 3 + 4 + 3 grouping by body, speech, mind is traditional; the verse does not state it). 'anyathā-kāma' is literally 'desire otherwise (than proper)'; commonly understood as improper sexual conduct, but the text does not say so. 'paruṣa' and 'anṛta' are given as two items (harsh speech, falsehood). The ten 'dharma-paths' are the avoidance of these sins, but the verse does not say it. The printed na of nābhyantarān is not translated (taken as a stray letter, see text_flags).

hindi: असंबद्ध बातचीत, द्वेष, लालसा और विपरीत दृष्टि — इस प्रकार दस तरह के पापकर्म को शरीर, वाणी और मन से छोड़ दे।
english: Incoherent talk, malice, covetousness and wrong view -- thus one should abandon sinful action, in its tenfold form, through body, speech and mind.
notes: Completes the list begun in unit 116 line 2: ten items (hiṃsā, steya, anyathākāma, paiśūnya, pāruṣya, anṛta, saṃbhinnālāpa, vyāpāda, abhidhyā, dṛgviparyaya). 'kāya-vāc-mānasaiḥ' = by the bodily, verbal, mental (acts). The verse could also be read as one sentence with unit 116.

words.gloss: of many harms, full of harms

hindi: दूसरों को चोट पहुँचाने वाले कर्म से धन का उपार्जन न करे। अनेक अनर्थों वाले धनों का देने वाला न होकर भी, क्योंकि असंभव होने से …
english: One should avoid earning wealth by action that injures others. Of riches full of many harms, even a non-giver, indeed, because of impossibility ... (sense of the second line uncertain).

text_flags.why: possible: 'adātā' (non-giver) gives no clear sense; 'ādātā' ('taker, acquirer') might fit better, but the avagraha in the print points to a-dātā; unresolved

notes: Line 1 is clear. Line 2 is not: the book's Hindi and English do not agree with each other or the Sanskrit. Literal: 'of riches (that are) full of many harms, even a non-giver (adātā), for impossibility'. Possible senses: even one who does not give away such riches is no better (since a good result is impossible), or the line says a giver of such riches cannot be. I do not settle it; the translation is deliberately literal and left open.

uncertain.note: [hindi/eng] Hindi ("अधर्म से धन कमाना असंभव") and English do not fit each other or Sanskrit `अदाताऽपि हि असंभवात्` — suggested: unclear

hindi: वह स्वर्ग, अपवर्ग और वैभवों को बिना प्रयास के प्राप्त कर लेता है। सायंकाल हल्का और हितकर भोजन करके, स्थिर मन वाला और पवित्र होकर,
english: He attains heaven, liberation and prosperities without effort. Having eaten in the evening a light, wholesome meal, with composed mind, pure,
notes: The subject of 'adhitiṣṭhati' (one who follows the above conduct) is not stated. 'svargāpavargavibhavān' read as a three-member dvandva (heaven, liberation, prosperities); it could be 'prosperities of heaven and liberation'. Line 2 starts a new sentence that continues in unit 120 ('having remembered the Instructor ... he should lie down'). 'bhuktvā' has the object 'laghu hitam' (meal, understood).
lines_deva: सायं भुक्त्वा लघु हितं समाहितमनाः शुचिः ॥
lines_iast: sāyaṃ bhuktvā laghu hitaṃ samāhitamanāḥ śuciḥ ||

words.gloss: having two or three trusted attendants

hindi: शास्ता का स्मरण करके फिर अपनी शय्या पर सोए — शुद्ध, भीड़रहित स्थान में, दो-तीन विश्वस्त परिचारकों के साथ।
english: Having remembered the Instructor (śāstṛ), he should then lie down on his own bed, in a clean, uncrowded place, with two or three trusted attendants.
notes: 'śāstṛ' is 'instructor, ruler, teacher'; the verse does not say whether a teacher or the deity is meant. Continues the sentence of unit 119 line 2.

hindi: उचित तकिये वाला, भली-भाँति बिछा हुआ, चौड़ा, समतल और सुखद, घुटने के बराबर ऊँचा, कोमल और शुभ शयन-आसन काम में ले।
english: One should use a bed-and-seat that has a suitable pillow, is well spread, wide, even and comfortable, knee-high, soft and auspicious.
notes: 'śayanāsana' read as 'bed and seat' (dvandva), i.e. a couch-bed. 'jānutulya' = of the height of the knee; the text says nothing more.

words.gloss: with head to the east or south

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. ātm. na+√kṛ

words.gloss: in the first and last part of the night

hindi: सिर पूर्व अथवा दक्षिण की ओर करके और पैरों को गुरुजनों की ओर न करते हुए, रात के पहले और पिछले भाग में धर्म का ही चिंतन करे।
english: With the head to the east or south, and not turning the feet towards elders, in the first and the last part of the night one should reflect on dharma alone.
notes: 'prāgdakṣiṇaśirāḥ' read as 'head to east or south' (could also be 'east and south', i.e. south-east). 'bhāge' is read as loc. sg. (collective 'portion'); a locative dual would be bhāgayoḥ, so 'bhāge' is read as locative singular; the sense 'first and last portion' comes from the dvandva pūrva-apara. The participles in line 1 qualify the sleeper; the only finite verb is 'anucintayet'. The sleeping verb is understood from units 120-121.

hindi: इस प्रकार सारहीन देह से सार को सदा ग्रहण करे; प्रतिक्षण मृत्यु से और अनुचित आचरण से डरता हुआ।
english: In this way one should always take the essence out of the body, from what is without essence; fearing at every moment death and improper conduct.
notes: 'bibhyat' takes the ablative: 'mṛtyoḥ' and 'ayathātatha-ceṣṭitāt' can be two things feared (as translated) or 'death resulting from improper conduct' (the book's reading). 'ayathātatha' = 'not as it should be' (improper); meaning of the compound is not certain. 'dehāt ... asārataḥ': 'from the body, from the essenceless'.

words.gloss: of one endowed with health, prosperity, wisdom, age, dharma, action

hindi: आरोग्य, वैभव, प्रज्ञा, वय और धर्मयुक्त कर्म से संपन्न पुरुष के लिए सुखमय और हितकर आयु कही गई है; विपरीत स्थिति में विपरीत।
english: For one endowed with health, prosperity, wisdom, age and dharmic action, a happy and beneficial lifespan is declared; the opposite in the opposite case.
notes: The compound can be segmented 'ārogya-vibhava-prajñā-vayaḥ' + 'dharma-kriyāvat' (as translated) or 'vayo-dharma' as 'age-appropriate duty'; the case of '-vataḥ' is read as genitive (for/of one who has). 'sukham āyuḥ hitam' = happy and beneficial life (two of the four kinds of life known in the tradition; the verse does not say so). 'viparītam viparyaye' = the opposite (unhappy, not beneficial) in the contrary case; the text leaves the content implied.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. caus. na+√duṣ

hindi: पृथ्वी पर राजा समस्त तेज का भंडार कहा जाता है। इसलिए मन को दूषित न करता हुआ, भक्ति से युक्त होकर उसकी सेवा करे।
english: On earth the king is called the repository of all splendour (tejas). Therefore, not corrupting the mind, being devoted, one should serve him.
notes: 'nṛpaityucyate' is printed with the vowels run together (nṛpa + iti), which strictly should stay apart; no change of sense. 'tejas' = splendour, majesty. 'adūṣayan manaḥ': whose mind (one's own, or the king's) is not stated; I keep it literal. 'bhaktimān' = devoted.

words.gloss: sitting in the paryastikā posture, leaning on a support, anger, laughter, quarrel, spitting, yawning

hindi: उसके समीप पर्यस्तिका आसन से बैठना, सहारा लेना, क्रोध और हँसी अथवा उपहास, विवाद, थूकना और जम्हाई लेना, तथा स्वभाव से अधिक सभी चेष्टाएँ छोड़ दे।
english: In his presence one should avoid sitting in the paryastikā posture, leaning on a support, anger and laughter (or perhaps mockery, upahāsa; see notes), quarrel, spitting and yawning, and all movements that exceed what is natural.
notes: The first line is a list of nouns whose verb is 'parivarjayet' in line 2; 'tat' (his) refers to the king of unit 125. 'kopahāsa' is read kopa + hāsa (anger, laughter), not 'upahāsa' (mockery) as the book's Hindi has; 'upāśraya' = support (to lean on) or recourse. 'paryastikā' is a particular way of sitting (legs drawn up and bound); I keep the name. 'prakṛti-abhyadhika' = beyond what is natural/usual (for the person). Alternative: the print also parses as ka + upahāsa (mockery), as the book's Hindi reads; both fit the syllable count, so 'anger, laughter' is not settled.

uncertain.note: [src] `कोपहास` vs Hindi उपहास — suggested: `पर्य्यस्तिकोपाश्रयहास...` or kept as कोप+हास

hindi: सभी अवस्थाएँ निश्चय ही अनेक प्रकार की होती हैं; उनमें से प्रत्येक अवस्था को भली-भाँति देखकर अपने हित का विधान करे। हितकारी उपदेशों में यहाँ जो कोई और मार्ग भी है, उसका भी सेवन करे।
english: All conditions are indeed of many kinds; having examined each of them properly, one should arrange what is good for oneself. Whatever other path there is here among beneficial teachings, one should follow that too.
notes: 'sarvā hy avasthā' is printed without the final visarga because it stands before a voiced letter (sandhi), so 'avasthāḥ' is correct. 'tāstāḥ' = tāḥ tāḥ ('each of those'). 'avasthā' = condition/situation (not specified). Upajāti metre (22 syllables a line).
lines_deva: सर्वाह्यवस्था विविधाश्च तास्ताः सम्यक् समीक्ष्यात्महितं विदध्यात् ॥
अन्योऽपि यः कश्चिदिहास्ति मार्गो हितोपदेशेषु भजेत तं च ॥
lines_iast: sarvāhyavasthā vividhāśca tāstāḥ samyak samīkṣyātmahitaṃ vidadhyāt ||
anyo'pi yaḥ kaścidihāsti mārgo hitopadeśeṣu bhajeta taṃ ca ||

words.gloss: one on whom all beings depend
whose mass of great virtues is renowned

hindi: इस प्रकार के आचरण से युक्त, सब जीवों का आश्रय, जिसके विशाल गुणों का समूह प्रसिद्ध है, देवताओं से रक्षित —
english: Thus, being endowed with this conduct, a support for all beings, with a renowned mass of great virtues, protected by the deities --
notes: GROUPING: this unit (3.252) and the next (3.253) are two halves of one verse; each line has 30 syllables and the whole fits a 15-syllable-pāda metre (mālinī-like). The input types them 'prose' but they are verse. The sentence continues in unit 129 with the main verb 'vrajati'. 'upajīvya' = one whom others live upon (a support).
lines_deva: इति चरितमुपेतः सर्वजीवोपजीव्यः प्रथितपृथुगुणौघो रक्षितो देवताभिः ॥
lines_iast: iti caritamupetaḥ sarvajīvopajīvyaḥ prathitapṛthuguṇaugho rakṣito devatābhiḥ ||

words.gloss: at the breaking up of the body

hindi: सौ वर्ष से अधिक जीने वाला, संतुष्ट, पुण्यकर्मा, सद्गति की ओर झुका हुआ वह देह के छूटने पर भी संतोष को प्राप्त होता है।
english: Living more than a hundred (years), content, of meritorious deeds, inclined towards a good state, he attains satisfaction even at the breaking up of the body.

text_flags.why: possible: the proofreading notes doubt 'sugatinimno ... tuṣṭiṃ' and suggest 'sugatiṃ ... tuṣṭaḥ'; the printed text is kept

notes: GROUPING: second half of the verse begun in unit 128 (see there); read the two together. The pipeline flags 'sugatinimno ... tuṣṭiṃ' and suggest 'sugatiṃ ... tuṣṭaḥ'; the printed text is intelligible and fits the metre, so I keep it ('sugati-nimna' = inclined to a good destination). 'vrajati tuṣṭiṃ' = goes to/attains contentment. 'samadhika-śata-jīvī' read as living over a hundred (years); 'years' is understood.
lines_deva: समधिकशतजीवी निर्वृतः पुण्यकर्मा व्रजति सुगतिनिम्नो देहभेदेऽपि तुष्टिं ॥
lines_iast: samadhikaśatajīvī nirvṛtaḥ puṇyakarmā vrajati sugatinimno dehabhede'pi tuṣṭiṃ ||

hindi: इस प्रकार दिनचर्या नामक तीसरा अध्याय। ३।
english: Thus the third chapter, named Dinacaryā (daily routine). 3.
notes: Closing colophon of chapter 3. 'iti ... adhyāyaḥ' with 'samāptaḥ' understood.
